memory_update.text: AVGO should remain a reference anchor rather than an underfollowed candidate; use it to trace custom AI accelerator and AI networking pull-through into substrates, advanced packaging, optical networking, switch ecosystems, power delivery, and test suppliers.

MU should remain a reference HBM anchor; its main Layer 2B value is mapping HBM capex and supply constraints into probe cards, wafer-level test, known-good-die, inspection, metrology, bonding, substrates, and advanced packaging.

TER is the most directly relevant underfollowed candidate in this chunk for semiconductor AI infrastructure because test intensity can rise with AI accelerator, HBM, and advanced-package complexity, but primary-source proof is still required.

CGNX and NOVT belong in an automation-components lane rather than a semiconductor bottleneck lane until filings show meaningful semiconductor/electronics, robotics, warehouse automation, or AI-enabled inspection exposure.

SYM belongs in a warehouse-automation systems lane with high deployment and customer-concentration diligence requirements; do not treat it as an AI infrastructure chokepoint without backlog quality and software-economics proof.

TENB and S are underfollowed cyber-control-plane hypotheses, but they require stricter evidence because software control planes are less physically scarce than chips, substrates, test, power, cooling, and electrical equipment.

NET and ZS should be retained as reference benchmarks for the cloud/cyber lane, not as underfollowed bottleneck names, unless future evidence shows AI workload monetization, mission-critical security dependence, and resilient retention.

Primary-source verification is missing for all names in this chunk. Next layer should pull 10-K/10-Q filings, earnings transcripts, investor decks, backlog/RPO data, segment revenue, customer concentration, AI-specific product disclosures, and margin trends.

Market-pricing checks are missing: current market cap, valuation multiples, revenue growth, margin expectations, analyst coverage, short interest, liquidity, and relative performance versus direct bottleneck peers need to be refreshed before prioritization.

Falsification triggers should include falling backlog or RPO, book-to-bill below 1 where applicable, AI revenue claims not converting to segment growth, margin compression, customer dual-sourcing, delayed hyperscaler capex, weaker DRAM/HBM pricing, and platform-vendor displacement in cyber.

summary: Layer 2B maps this candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships rather than rankings. The reference lane contains Broadcom, Micron, Cloudflare, and Zscaler as visible anchors for custom AI silicon, HBM, networking, cloud, and security control-plane demand. The underfollowed lane contains Teradyne, Cognex, Novanta, Symbotic, Tenable, and SentinelOne, but most of these remain hypotheses because the provided evidence does not yet prove direct AI infrastructure bottleneck status. Stronger cached evidence supports second-order semiconductor and physical-infrastructure bottlenecks around HBM, advanced packaging, test, MLCCs, substrates, switchgear, power, and chemicals; evidence for automation and cyber names is currently more thematic and requires filing-level validation.
